source_snapshot.message:
fix(php): scope use-clause parsing to the clause, not the statement

Two defects, one root cause: both the query and the alias flag looked at the
whole 'use' declaration instead of the individual clause.

1. Phantom imports. In 'use Vendor[local-path]\User as Admin' the alias is a
   direct (name) sibling of the (qualified_name), so the unanchored
   alternation captured it as a second imported module. Ix then matched
   'Admin' against an unrelated class of that name, emitting an IMPORTS edge
   the file never declares and promoting the wrong short-name matches from
   0.5 to 0.9 — the exact class of error this PR exists to remove. Anchoring
   the capture to the clause's first named child fixes it; a bare
   'use GlobalThing;' is a lone (name) child and still matches.

2. Comma-separated imports. importAliased came from a regex over the whole
   statement, so 'use A[local-path]\Alpha, A[local-path]\Beta as Bee;' flagged every clause
   as aliased and silently disabled FQCN resolution for Alpha. Reading the
   clause node instead scopes it correctly.

Deriving the flag from the node also deletes an unanchored /[local-path]\s+/ over
repo-controlled text — the same polynomial-backtracking class CodeQL flagged
at phpTypeFqcn, in a spot it did not flag. Measured at ~3.7s on a use
statement padded with 100k spaces, which parses as valid PHP.

The two anchored kind regexes (^use function, ^use const) are linear and
unchanged.

core-ingestion: 334 passed, 6 pre-existing failures unchanged from base.
